key_factors: Pre-formed heat sink components (fins, heat pipe, vapor chamber, base, copper plate)
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the dedicated thermal module components in China
flip: Fabricating and forming the aluminum fins, copper heat pipes, and vapor chambers from raw metal materials in Mexico prior to soldering
reasoning: All components of the thermal modules are manufactured in China with a predetermined end-use as parts of a CPU heat sink assembly. The operations in Mexico—applying solder paste, arranging pre-formed components in a fixture, oven soldering, testing, and applying thermal grease—constitute simple assembly. Unlike N330771 or N316151 where key components were fabricated in Mexico, the Chinese components here already possess the essential character of the thermal modules and do not undergo a substantial transformation in Mexico.

key_factors: Aluminum alloy sheet in coils
decisive_step: Rolling and manufacturing of the aluminum alloy sheets in China
flip: Combining the cut aluminum panels with polystyrene and forming them into dedicated swimming pool wall panels in Canada prior to U.S. importation
reasoning: Consistent with N316637 and N316780, the essential character of the imported article is imparted by the Chinese aluminum sheet. The operations performed in Canada—slitting, painting, de-coiling, cutting-to-size, and corner notching—are minor finishing and sizing operations that do not change the fundamental character or tariff classification (heading 7606) of the aluminum sheet into a dedicated pool part. Thus, no substantial transformation occurs in Canada, and the country of origin remains China.

key_factors: MDF back panel and acrylic face panel
decisive_step: Manufacturing and drilling of the MDF and acrylic panels in Canada
flip: Manufacturing and pre-drilling the MDF and acrylic panels in China while only applying the decorative vinyl skin and packaging the kit in Canada
reasoning: Following the prior determination for the base kit in N336902, the essential character of the wall-mounted wine rack is imparted by the structural panels (MDF and acrylic) manufactured in Canada, rather than the aluminum pegs or hardware. Applying a decorative vinyl skin to the acrylic panel in Canada is a minor finishing operation that merely enhances aesthetic appeal and does not alter the Canada origin already conferred by the production of the structural panels.

key_factors: Filter media / mesh jacket
decisive_step: Manufacturing and swaging the multi-layer filtration mesh jacket in Country A
flip: Fabricating and swaging the filtration mesh jacket layers in Canada rather than importing the completed cartridge from Country A
reasoning: The proMESH is a sand control filter classified in subheading 8421.29.00. As stated in the facts, the filter media (mesh jacket) is the core of the sand control mechanism and imparts the essential character of the filtering apparatus. The mesh jacket is completely manufactured in Country A (wrapping multiple filtration layers, swaging into a cartridge, and welding end rings). Processing in Canada—drilling the base pipe, pushing the jacket and centralizer onto the pipe, and welding—does not substantially transform the Country A filter cartridge.

key_factors: Maceration with juniper and botanicals and redistillation into gin
decisive_step: Macerating neutral grain alcohol with botanicals and distilling in Canada
flip: Perform the botanical maceration and distillation in the Netherlands and only dilute with water and bottle in Canada
reasoning: Neutral grain alcohol from the Netherlands and Canada (HTS 2207.10) is macerated with juniper berries and other botanicals and redistilled in Canada to remove impurities and produce gin (HTS 2208.50). This distillation process changes the raw material's name, character, and use—transforming unflavored neutral spirits into a distinct alcoholic beverage (gin) and satisfying the Part 102 tariff shift rules used for USMCA marking.

key_factors: Photovoltaic solar cells
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the crystalline silicon solar cells in China
flip: Manufacturing the photovoltaic solar cells from silicon wafers in Mexico
reasoning: Consistent with CBP precedent (e.g., H266527 and N303846), the photovoltaic solar cells impart the essential character to a solar panel. The assembly of foreign-sourced solar cells (typically from China) with glass, frames, and junction boxes into finished solar panels in Mexico is considered a simple assembly operation that does not substantially transform the solar cells. Therefore, the country of origin remains the country where the solar cells were manufactured.

key_factors: Blending and processing of cane sugar, water, maple syrups, and flavorings into a finished table syrup
decisive_step: Formulating, processing, and retail bottling of the syrup blend in Canada
flip: If the syrup were merely a simple dilution of imported cane sugar with water without creating a new food preparation under heading 2106, origin would remain with the country of the cane sugar.
reasoning: For USMCA marking purposes, CBP applies the tariff shift rules in 19 C.F.R. Part 102. Under 19 C.F.R. § 102.11(a)(3), when foreign (e.g., cane sugar of heading 1701) and domestic ingredients (maple syrup, water, flavorings) are processed and blended in Canada to create a retail food preparation classified in heading 2106, all foreign ingredients undergo the required tariff shift under 19 C.F.R. § 102.20 (consistent with N328973, N320159, and N326397). Thus, the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: Blending and processing of cereal ingredients into a prepared cereal food (heading 1904)
decisive_step: Processing and combining the multi-country ingredients into a prepared cereal in Canada
flip: If the US-origin cereal flakes (already classified in heading 1904) failed to undergo a tariff shift and imparted the essential character under 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1), origin would be the United States.
reasoning: For USMCA marking purposes, CBP applies the Part 102 tariff-shift rules (as in N317341 and N320159). Prepared cereals are classified in heading 1904. The Rule for 1904.20/1904.90 under 19 CFR 102.20 requires a change to heading 1904 from any other heading (or chapters). All foreign ingredients shift from other chapters (e.g., 08, 11, 12, 15, 20) into heading 1904 in Canada. Even if US cereal flakes do not shift, the mixed cereal takes Canada origin via tariff shift or substantial transformation in Canada.

key_factors: Cover Casting and Main Board Casting
decisive_step: Casting and forming of the main aluminum castings in South Korea
flip: Casting and forming the Cover Casting and Main Board Casting in Mexico instead of South Korea
reasoning: The Cover Casting and Main Board Casting impart the essential character of the aluminum adapter plate assembly by forming the structural mounting plate and fluid conduits. These castings are produced to their dedicated shape and form in South Korea. In Mexico, the castings are merely combined with a gasket, dowel pins, and threaded fasteners. Following CBP precedent such as H312745, this simple screw-and-pin assembly does not constitute a substantial transformation, leaving the country of origin as South Korea.

key_factors: perforated LDPE drip lines
decisive_step: Manufacturing and perforating the LDPE drip lines in the United States
flip: Manufacturing the LDPE drip lines in Mexico or extruding the components in Mexico prior to fusion
reasoning: The IMT is a composite good whose primary function is distributing leaching agents, meaning the US-origin perforated LDPE drip lines impart the essential character. Under both the substantial transformation test and 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1) (similar to N262359), the assembly operations in Mexico—perforating sleeves, feeding drip lines into sleeves, and thermo-fusing them to Chilean LDPE film—constitute simple assembly and do not substantially transform the pre-perforated US drip lines.

key_factors: Complex assembly of the rack, pinion, inner/outer ball joints, and housing into a complete steering mechanism
decisive_step: Final assembly and integration of multi-country steering components into the Manual Rack and Pinion Gear in Mexico
flip: Importing the rack, pinion, and housing already pre-assembled as a complete gear subassembly from China or South Korea and only attaching minor brackets or boots in Mexico
reasoning: Consistent with H315296 and N335654, combining numerous mechanical components sourced from multiple countries (China, South Korea, Indonesia, Mexico, and Poland)—including the pinion gear, rack gear, inner ball joints, and outer ball joints—into a complete automotive Manual Rack and Pinion Gear in Mexico constitutes a substantial transformation. No single imported part has the character of the finished steering assembly prior to the Mexican manufacturing operations.

key_factors: Blending of multi-sourced chemical and mineral inputs into a specialized drilling fluid additive (tariff shift to heading 3824)
decisive_step: Mixing and blending of raw materials in Canada satisfying the Part 102 tariff shift rules for marking
flip: If the finished product were classified in heading 2710 (same as the 50.75% U.S. mineral oil) or if the mixing were evaluated solely under non-preferential substantial transformation without Part 102 marking rules, origin could be the United States or China.
reasoning: Because the processing occurs in Canada, marking origin is determined under 19 CFR Part 102 (see N318582, N335182). Lubrigel L is a prepared drilling fluid additive classified in heading 3824. Since all foreign and U.S. inputs are classified in other headings (2710, 3402, 6806, 3913, 1302), the blending in Canada satisfies the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule (or 102.11(d)(3) last country of production), conferring Canadian origin for marking purposes.

key_factors: Scallop medallions
decisive_step: Harvesting and forming the scallops into medallions in China
flip: If the scallops were harvested in Chapter 03 and both formed into medallions and wrapped in bacon in Canada, causing a tariff shift into Chapter 16 in Canada.
reasoning: For non-preferential purposes (Section 301), CBP applies the substantial transformation test. Simply wrapping frozen Chinese scallop medallions in raw bacon in Canada is a minor assembly/finishing operation that does not change the fundamental character of the scallops, which impart the essential character to the dish. Note that while N326450 assigned Canadian origin for marking under 19 CFR Part 102 tariff-shift rules, under the traditional substantial transformation test (and 19 CFR 102.11(b) if medallions enter under heading 1605), origin remains China.

key_factors: Aluminum structural components (posts, tracks, beams) and fabric canopy manufactured in Canada
decisive_step: Extrusion, cutting, welding, and painting of aluminum billets into structural components, along with cutting and sewing the fabric canopy in Canada
flip: If the aluminum components were extruded, welded, and finished in Turkey and the fabric canopy was cut and sewn in the U.S., with only simple kitting or packaging occurring in Canada.
reasoning: Following N325521 and N326606, extruding, cutting, and finishing Turkish aluminum billets in Canada substantially transforms them into new structural components. Additionally, U.S. fabric is cut and sewn into a fitted canopy in Canada, and the aluminum parts undergo welding, tapping, and painting there. Because both the essential aluminum structure and the textile canopy are manufactured and combined in Canada from raw materials, the components undergo a substantial transformation in Canada, making it the country of origin.

key_factors: The 8mm-thick hevea plywood substrate (heading 4412)
decisive_step: Manufacture of the multi-ply plywood substrate in Indonesia
flip: Importing individual wood veneers into Canada and laminating all plies together into plywood in Canada
reasoning: Unlike USMCA marking rules (19 CFR 102.20) in N335201 where profiling edges into flooring satisfies a tariff shift within heading 4412 for marking only, non-preferential origin for duty purposes relies on substantial transformation. Under CBP precedent, an imported plywood substrate (4412.31) already possesses the essential character of a laminated wood panel. Bonding a face ply, tongue-and-groove profiling, and UV coating in Canada merely finish the panel into flooring without changing its fundamental character or tariff heading, leaving origin in Indonesia.

key_factors: forged and machined inner and outer toothed races
decisive_step: forging, turning, and gear-tooth cutting of the bearing rings in China
flip: Perform the forging, ring machining, and gear-tooth cutting of the races in the country of final assembly
reasoning: Under HQ 083066, slewing rings with gear teeth are classified as gears under heading 8483 because the toothed races perform the principal gearing function while rolling elements merely reduce friction. Consistent with CBP bearings and gears rulings (e.g., N318162, N317669), the inner and outer toothed rings impart the essential character. Simple assembly of balls/rollers, cages, and seals into pre-machined, pre-toothed races from China does not result in a substantial transformation, leaving China as the country of origin.

key_factors: Aluminum wine pegs
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the aluminum wine pegs in India
flip: Manufacturing the aluminum wine pegs and machining the MDF/acrylic panels in Canada instead of importing the pre-made pegs from India.
reasoning: Following precedent N337479 (and N336902), which involved the 3-foot version of the identical VINdustry peg and panel kit with the same component and value ratios, the aluminum wine pegs impart the essential character to the disassembled wine rack kit because they directly support the wine bottles. Affixing a decorative vinyl skin to the acrylic panel and packaging the components in Canada does not constitute a substantial transformation. Therefore, the country of origin remains India, where the pegs are manufactured.

key_factors: PCBA, imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge subassemblies manufactured and integrated in Mexico
decisive_step: Manufacture of the PCBA, imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge in Mexico, combined with firmware installation and final assembly with the Chinese printer transport
flip: Manufacturing the imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge in China as part of the imported printer transport (as in H304677)
reasoning: Distinguishing HQ H304677, where the Chinese printer transport contained nearly all mechanical printing components and only the PCBA was made in Mexico, here the transport lacks key mechanical printing assemblies. In Mexico, Lexmark manufactures the PCBA (via SMT/PTH), imaging unit, developing unit, and toner cartridge (accounting for 61% of total labor hours), downloads U.S.-designed firmware, and integrates them with the Chinese transport. This complex manufacturing and assembly substantially transforms the components into finished printers of Mexican origin.

key_factors: Fabrication of the stainless steel band and housing
decisive_step: Slitting, progressive die stamping, forming, and perforating raw steel coils into bands and housings in Canada, followed by final assembly
flip: If the bands and housings were pre-formed in India or China and merely assembled with the screw in Canada
reasoning: In Canada, raw flat coiled stainless steel from India undergoes more than mere slitting (distinguishing N316637); it is slit, fed into progressive dies, formed, and precisely perforated to create dedicated hose clamp bands and housings, then assembled with a Chinese screw. Similar to N334104, fabricating raw steel stock into identifiable components and assembling them into a finished product constitutes a substantial transformation into a new article with a distinct name, character, and use, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: Conversion of raw plastic film rolls and spouts into finished, heat-sealed packaging pouches
decisive_step: Cutting, heat-sealing the polyethylene film into pouches, and incorporating the spouts in Mexico
flip: If the pouches were already pre-formed and heat-sealed in China, and only the spouts were inserted in Mexico.
reasoning: In China, the components are merely printed polyethylene film in rolls (heading 3920/3921) and plastic spouts. In Mexico, the film is unwound, precisely cut, heat-sealed into shapes, and fitted with spouts to create finished articles for the conveyance or packing of goods (heading 3923). This manufacturing process results in a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use, constituting a substantial transformation in Mexico (And satisfying the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift for marking).

key_factors: Extruded and fabricated aluminum structural posts and beams
decisive_step: Extrusion, cutting, tapping, welding, and powder coating of Turkish aluminum billets in Canada
flip: If the aluminum profiles were already extruded to shape in Turkey and only cut to length, tapped, and powder-coated in Canada, origin would remain Turkey.
reasoning: Consistent with rulings N339969, N325521, and N326606, extruding raw aluminum billets into structural profiles and further fabricating them (cutting, tapping holes, welding base plates, and powder coating) in Canada substantially transforms the Turkish billets into a new and different article of commerce—an unassembled aluminum canopy structure—with a distinct name, character, and use. Therefore, the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: Forged and heat-treated valve blank
decisive_step: Electric upsetting, extrusion, and heat treatment of bar stock into valve blanks in China
flip: Perform the electric upsetting, extrusion (forging), and heat treatment of the raw bar stock in Mexico instead of China
reasoning: In China, raw cylindrical bar stock undergoes electric upsetting, extrusion, and heat treatments (hardening/tempering/aging) to create a rough valve blank with the predetermined shape, metallurgical properties, and dedicated use of an engine valve. The subsequent processing in Mexico—comprising turning, rough and finish grinding, chrome plating, polishing, and inspection—merely refines and finishes the existing blank into final tolerances without changing its fundamental character, name, or use. Therefore, no substantial transformation occurs in Mexico, and the origin remains China.

key_factors: The base paper or polypropylene film coated with adhesive and laminated to release paper
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the jumbo rolls of self-adhesive labelstock in China
flip: Manufacturing the base paper/film and performing the adhesive coating and laminating in the third country (e.g., Vietnam or Mexico) rather than merely slitting jumbo rolls from China
reasoning: Based on direct precedent N341007 involving identical merchandise (thermal paper, semi-gloss paper, and polypropylene self-adhesive labelstock imported in 10 to 22-inch rolls), the essential character is imparted by the production, adhesive-coating, and lamination of the jumbo labelstock rolls in China. Subsequent slitting and cutting of the jumbo rolls into narrower rolls in a third country constitutes mere finishing and does not result in a substantial transformation.

key_factors: Surface-treated titanium dioxide pigment
decisive_step: Dispersion, chemical surface treatment, drying, and grinding in Canada, converting crude titanium dioxide (2823) into pigment (3206.11)
flip: Perform the chemical surface treatment in China, leaving only drying, grinding, or simple packaging in Canada.
reasoning: In China, Egyptian ilmenite is refined into raw titanium dioxide (HTSUS 2823.00). In Canada, this intermediate undergoes dispersion, chemical surface treatment, drying, and grinding to produce finished Titanium Dioxide Pigment (HTSUS 3206.11). This surface treatment imparts the specific properties required for paint/coating applications, resulting in a new article with a distinct name, character, and use (substantial transformation for Section 301) and satisfying the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift from heading 2823 to 3206.11 for USMCA marking (analogous to N334326).

key_factors: Magnetic tape storage modules (Base, Cartridge Expansion, I/E Expansion, Drive Expansion) and integrated robotic mechanism
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the storage modules and final integration, electrical interconnection, and assembly into the rack cabinet in Mexico
flip: If the pre-assembled storage modules and tape drives were completely manufactured in China and merely mounted into the rack in Mexico
reasoning: The Serverless Rack (Osmium 45U Stack) is produced by BDT de México. As established in related ruling NY N342790, the core functional components—the nine magnetic tape storage modules (Base, Cartridge, I/E, and Drive Expansions) and the internal robotic mechanism—impart the essential character of the mass data storage unit. Their manufacture and complex physical and electrical integration into the cabinet in Mexico substantially transform the individual subcomponents into a new article of commerce.

key_factors: The rough steel forgings already formed into the dedicated shapes of flanges, crosses, and tees
decisive_step: Heating, forging into rough shapes, and heat-treating the steel billets in China, Italy, or India
flip: Importing raw steel billets or bars into Mexico and performing the closed-die forging and heat treatment in Mexico
reasoning: Under CBP precedent (e.g., Midwood Industries), rough forgings already possessing the approximate size, shape, and metallurgy of the finished flanges and fittings have a predetermined end use and essential character. The subsequent operations in Mexico—CNC machining, drilling, boring, beveling, threading, and painting—are considered finishing operations that bring the rough forgings to final tolerances without changing their fundamental name, character, or use. Thus, origin remains China (or Italy/India, depending on where forged).

key_factors: Bicycle frame
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the bicycle frame in China
flip: Manufacturing the bicycle frame in Taiwan or Canada instead of China
reasoning: In CBP rulings involving bicycles assembled in Canada from foreign components (e.g., N295820 and H302204), simple assembly of pre-manufactured bicycle parts of heading 8714 does not result in a substantial transformation or satisfy the tariff shift rules under 19 CFR 102.20 (8712 requires a shift from any heading except 8714). Under both substantial transformation and 19 CFR 102.11(b)(1), the bicycle frame imparts the essential character of a bicycle. Thus, the country where the frame is manufactured (China) confers origin.

key_factors: Thermal bending, annealing, and laminating flat glass into a curved safety windshield
decisive_step: Heating, mold-pressing (bending), annealing, and laminating the flat glass in Mexico
flip: If the glass were already bent, tempered/annealed, and laminated into a curved windshield blank in China, and only sensors, brackets, and pins were attached in Mexico.
reasoning: Flat glass sheets from China undergo a complex thermal manufacturing process in Mexico, including heating to 634°C, press-bending on a mold along two axes, annealing for strength, and lamination, followed by attaching sensors and brackets. Under longstanding CBP precedent, converting raw flat glass into bent, laminated automotive safety glass creates a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use (an automotive windshield), substantially transforming the Chinese flat glass in Mexico.

key_factors: The pure nickel powder produced by hydrometallurgy
decisive_step: Hydrometallurgical manufacturing of the nickel powder in Australia
flip: If the Canadian processing chemically altered the nickel powder or alloyed it into a distinct metal article rather than merely screening and sizing it
reasoning: The nickel powder is completely manufactured by hydrometallurgy in Australia, imparting its essential character as 100% pure nickel powder (subheading 7504.00.00, HTSUS). In Canada, the powder is merely screened, cut into different particle sizes, blended by size, and packaged. Under both the substantial transformation test and the Part 102 marking rules for USMCA goods (where no tariff shift occurs within 7504.00.00), mere sizing, screening, and blending do not create a new article of commerce, leaving origin as Australia.

key_factors: Formed cylindrical steel battery can housing
decisive_step: Deep-drawing, stamping, forming of Korean steel and assembly with rivet and gasket in Mexico
flip: If the cylindrical steel can were already stamped and formed in Korea, with only minor assembly of the rivet and gasket occurring in Mexico
reasoning: Raw steel (Chapter 72) and minor hardware from Korea are processed in Mexico to produce the 4680 Cylindrical Can Assembly classified under subheading 8507.90.8000, HTSUS. Forming raw steel into a dedicated cylindrical battery housing and assembling it with a rivet and gasket substantially transforms the raw materials into a new article with a distinct name, character, and use (and satisfies the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule for marking, similar to N320075). Thus, origin is Mexico.

key_factors: The tapered roller bearing cone (or the combination of the Indian bearing cone and Taiwanese oil seal, with India predominating)
decisive_step: Machining, grinding, polishing, heat treatment, and assembly of the steel tapered roller bearing cone in India
flip: Manufacturing the tapered roller bearing cone in Taiwan, Mexico, or China alongside more complex machining operations during final assembly.
reasoning: Simply pressing the Taiwanese oil seal onto the Indian tapered roller bearing cone (even with >1,000 ft-lbs of force) is a simple assembly of two finished components with predetermined end-uses and does not constitute a substantial transformation in Taiwan, Mexico, or China. Because the assembly is not substantially transformed during final press-fitting, origin rests with the country imparting the primary mechanical component and highest value/complexity, which is the precision-ground and heat-treated steel bearing cone made in India.

key_factors: Galvanized and painted flat-rolled nonalloy steel coils
decisive_step: Melting, pouring, rolling, galvanizing, and painting of the steel coils in Brazil
flip: Further fabricating, drilling, punching, and assembling the sheets in Mexico into identifiable structural parts classified in heading 7308
reasoning: The steel is melted, poured, hot-dip galvanized, and painted into flat-rolled coils in Brazil, imparting its fundamental material properties and essential character. In Mexico, the coils are merely roll-formed into angular profile sheets (classified in heading 7216) and cut to length. Under CBP precedent and Part 102 rules (where flat-rolled steel of 7210/7212 to angles/shapes of 7216 fails the tariff shift rule unless from 7208/7209/7211), simple roll-forming and cutting to length do not constitute a substantial transformation.

key_factors: Japanese-origin thermoplastic vulcanizate (TPV) base polymer
decisive_step: Production of the TPV base polymer in Japan
flip: Perform a chemical reaction (such as dynamic vulcanization or polymerization of monomers) during the processing in China, Taiwan, or Mexico rather than simple physical blending.
reasoning: The Japanese-origin TPV (approx. 63.5% by weight) imparts the essential character of the finished propylene elastomer pellets. The melting, physical mixing/blending with mineral oil and minor additives, and pelletizing in China, Taiwan, or Mexico do not result in a chemical reaction or change the fundamental character and use of the base polymer. Because mere physical compounding and pelletizing of an existing polymer do not constitute a substantial transformation, the country of origin remains Japan.

key_factors: The wound stator, centrifugally cast rotor, and assembled mechanical compression unit
decisive_step: Manufacturing the stator and rotor from raw materials and assembling/welding the complete hermetic compressor in Mexico
flip: Importing pre-manufactured stators, rotors, and pre-assembled mechanical pump subassemblies from China for simple housing enclosure in Mexico
reasoning: Consistent with H315287 and H318255, the foreign components undergo a substantial transformation in Mexico. In Mexico, raw lamination sheets, magnet wire, and aluminum ingot are manufactured into the core motor components (stator and rotor) via stacking, coil winding, forming, and centrifugal casting. These are then integrated with the crankshaft, piston, valves, and welded housing across 86 complex operations to create a new article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use.

key_factors: Preparation, assembly, and tariff shift of multi-origin food ingredients into a finished frozen breakfast wrap
decisive_step: Combining, assembling, wrapping, and freezing the diverse ingredients into the finished food preparation in Canada
flip: If the wraps were fully assembled in the United States and merely frozen and packaged in Canada
reasoning: Consistent with precedents N320159 and N325186, country of origin marking for USMCA imports is determined under the 19 C.F.R. Part 102 tariff shift rules, which codify the substantial transformation test. The non-Canadian ingredients (such as U.S. lavash, Greek spinach, and spices) undergo the requisite tariff shift under 19 C.F.R. § 102.20 when combined with Canadian egg and cheese components and assembled into a new article of commerce (a frozen breakfast wrap, heading 1905 or 2106) in Canada, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: Finished upholstered office chair structure, cushioning, and textile assembly
decisive_step: Manufacturing, upholstery, and packaging of the foreign and domestic components into a complete unassembled chair in Mexico
flip: If the chair's metal/plastic frames, casters, gas lift, and cut-and-sewn upholstery were all manufactured in China and merely kitted/packaged together in Mexico without manufacturing or upholstery operations
reasoning: Following the pattern in the cited USMCA/Section 301 rulings (e.g., N319373, N317251), the requester seeks USMCA eligibility and confirmation that China Section 301 duties do not apply. The foreign (likely Chinese) raw materials and components undergo substantial transformation—and satisfy Part 102 / USMCA tariff shift rules for heading 9401—through fabrication, upholstery, and production operations in Mexico to create the complete WP1000 Mesh Chair.

key_factors: Standardbred horse semen
decisive_step: Production and veterinary collection of the semen from stallions in Canada
flip: If the semen were collected from stallions in a third country and merely repackaged into syringes in Canada.
reasoning: The subject merchandise is Standardbred horse semen collected from stallions and packaged in syringes in Canada. As a natural animal product wholly obtained or produced in a single country, its essential character is entirely imparted by the biological production and collection in Canada (19 CFR 102.11(a)(1) / wholly obtained). Packaging into syringes and Styrofoam boxes does not alter the origin.

key_factors: Formed and cured carbon fiber rim structure
decisive_step: Cutting, laminating on molds, curing in an oven, and drilling of carbon fiber sheets in Canada
flip: Import pre-molded and cured carbon fiber rim blanks from the United States and only perform spoke-hole drilling and finishing in Canada.
reasoning: U.S.-sourced raw carbon fiber sheets and epoxy resin are imported into Canada, where they undergo complex manufacturing—including CNC cutting, laminating onto molds, vacuum debulking, oven curing, and spoke-hole drilling. Similar to N320075 and H329175, processing raw bulk materials into a finished structural component creates a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use (bicycle rims). Thus, substantial transformation occurs in Canada.

key_factors: Bulk Parmesan cheese wheels
decisive_step: Production of the Parmesan cheese from milk in the United States
flip: Producing the bulk Parmesan cheese wheels from milk in Canada rather than the United States
reasoning: The bulk Parmesan cheese wheels are produced in the United States (Wisconsin), which imparts the essential character of the product. The subsequent operations in Canada—shredding or shaving the cheese, applying a U.S.-origin anticaking agent, and retail packaging—are minor processing steps that do not change the fundamental character, name, or use of the cheese. Neither substantial transformation nor a qualifying tariff shift under 19 C.F.R. 102.20 occurs in Canada, so the country of origin remains the United States.

key_factors: Conversion of raw sodium bentonite clay, limestone, and dedusting agent into cat litter
decisive_step: Mixing raw clay with limestone and dedusting agent and packaging in Canada
flip: Processing and formulating the sodium bentonite clay into usable cat litter in the United States prior to shipping to Canada for mere packaging
reasoning: Under the substantial transformation test and 19 C.F.R. 102.11(a)(3) (for USMCA marking), raw unprocessed sodium bentonite clay (heading 2508) mined in the U.S. undergoes a tariff shift and substantial transformation in Canada when mixed with Canadian limestone and a dedusting agent to create a new article of commerce: retail cat litter (heading 3824). Similar to N317341 and N320151, blending raw ingredients in Canada into a distinct finished product confers Canadian origin.

key_factors: Xanthan Gum (functional viscosifier additive)
decisive_step: Production of Xanthan Gum in China
flip: If the mixing in Canada involved a complex chemical reaction rather than simple suspension blending, or if the Xanthan Gum was sourced from the United States or Canada.
reasoning: Under the substantial transformation test (and 19 CFR 102.21/102.11 exceptions for simple mixing), mere blending of ingredients in Canada to suspend xanthan gum in a mineral oil carrier does not result in a substantial transformation. Unlike H334088 (which addressed USMCA marking via tariff shift), for non-preferential Section 301 purposes, simple mixing does not confer origin. The Chinese xanthan gum is the highest-cost component and the sole functional additive imparting the essential character (viscosifying properties) to the drilling fluid additive.

key_factors: Fabrication of the steel mower deck, handrails, molded components, and final integration with the engine
decisive_step: Stamping and forming the steel mower deck and handrails, plastic molding, and final assembly in Mexico
flip: Importing the stamped mower deck, handrails, and engine pre-manufactured from China for simple bolt-together assembly in Mexico
reasoning: In Mexico, raw Mexican steel and plastic are substantially transformed via hydraulic pressing, CNC cutting, bending, and injection molding into major structural components (mower deck, handrails, wheels, guards). These key components are then assembled with a U.S.-origin engine and Chinese parts (blades, axles, hardware) into a finished walk-behind lawn mower. The extensive fabrication of the core structural body alongside final assembly in Mexico creates a new article with a distinct name, character, and use.

key_factors: The 12 VDC brushed electric motor (along with the gearbox, screw drive, and sensor PCBA)
decisive_step: Manufacture of the DC motor and key subassemblies in China
flip: Manufacturing the DC motor from its constituent parts (stator, rotor, windings) in Canada
reasoning: The finished electric actuator is classified in heading 8501 as an electric motor. Its essential character is imparted by the 12 VDC motor, which is fully produced in China along with the gearbox, screw drive, housings, and sensor PCBA. Unlike N301975 and N316151 where core motor subassemblies were manufactured in the assembly country, the Canadian operations here consist merely of simple fastening, soldering wires, and testing, which do not substantially transform the Chinese motor.

key_factors: Canadian-manufactured PVC plastic extrusions and injection-molded earring holders
decisive_step: Plastic extrusion, injection molding, and wrapping/assembly into the finished jewelry organizer tray in Canada
flip: If the PVC profile extrusions and molded earring holders were manufactured in China and merely wrapped or packaged in Canada
reasoning: The jewelry organizer tray's structural identity and essential character are imparted by the large and medium PVC u-shaped extrusions and the injection-molded earring trays, all manufactured in Canada. In Canada, Chinese roll PVC fabric is substantially transformed when cut, glued, and wrapped onto the Canadian extrusions, which are then combined with the Canadian earring trays and Chinese foam ring holder. Because the core structural components and final assembly occur in Canada, the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: Aluminum diecast armature and polyurethane (PU) base wheel
decisive_step: Manufacturing the aluminum diecast armature and PU base in the United States
flip: Manufacturing the aluminum diecast armature and PU base wheel in Mexico instead of the United States.
reasoning: The aluminum diecast armature and polyurethane base wheel manufactured in the United States already possess the essential character, form, and function of a steering wheel. The operations in Mexico—cutting and sewing leather, installing heating elements, and inserting wood trim—are finishing and assembly operations that do not change the fundamental character or use of the U.S.-origin base wheel, and therefore do not constitute a substantial transformation.

key_factors: Assembly of structural wall, floor, roof, and frame subassemblies into a complete truck cargo body
decisive_step: Seven-step structural assembly and riveting of the cargo container in Mexico
flip: If the major structural subassemblies were all imported from a single non-Mexican country as a complete knockdown kit and merely bolted together in Mexico
reasoning: In Mexico, discrete structural parts and subassemblies (walls, floor, roof, rails, rear frame, door, and electrical harness) are joined and riveted in a seven-step process to construct a complete heavy-truck cargo body (heading 8707). Consistent with H314637, this comprehensive structural assembly substantially transforms the individual parts (all non-USMCA materials being outside heading 8707) into a new article with a distinct name, character, and use. Subsequent mounting onto trucks in the U.S. occurs post-importation.

key_factors: Finished multi-pair insulated data cable structure
decisive_step: Wire drawing, annealing, primary insulation extrusion, pair twisting, and outer jacket extrusion in Mexico
flip: Importing finished bulk CAT6 cable into Mexico where it is merely cut to length, tested, and spooled onto reels
reasoning: In Mexico, raw copper wire (from Taiwan or the U.S.) and raw insulation resins (from Japan and China) undergo complex manufacturing: wire drawing, annealing, primary extrusion, pair twisting, and outer jacket extrusion. Consistent with N310624, converting raw wire and insulating materials into a finished multi-conductor data cable (HTSUS 8544.49) constitutes a substantial transformation into a new article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use, conferring Mexican origin for both scenarios.

key_factors: Combined metal leg assembly and plastic seat/backrest shell
decisive_step: Manufacturing and assembly of the Chinese metal leg assembly and U.S. plastic shell into a complete chair in Mexico
flip: If both the metal leg assembly and the plastic seat shell were sourced from China and merely fastened together in Mexico, the origin would be China.
reasoning: Neither the Chinese metal leg assembly nor the U.S. plastic seat shell alone imparts the essential character of the finished stacking chair; both are equally critical structural components classified as parts (9401.99). Consistent with N345246, where Chinese components were combined with non-Chinese seating components in Mexico, assembling the distinct U.S. and Chinese structural halves in Mexico substantially transforms the parts into a new article of commerce (a complete seat under 9401.79) and satisfies 19 C.F.R. 102.20 tariff shift rules.

key_factors: Agglomerated potato flakes
decisive_step: Production of the agglomerated potato flakes in the United States
flip: Manufacturing the potato flakes in Canada, or cooking/processing raw potatoes into prepared flakes in Canada
reasoning: The agglomerated potato flakes from the United States impart the essential character to the instant mashed potato mix. Merely weighing, dry-blending, and packaging pre-made potato flakes with sea salt and butter powder in Canada constitutes simple mixing that does not result in a substantial transformation into a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, or use (nor does it satisfy the tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) from heading 1105 to 2005 due to 102.17).

key_factors: Brake caliper core
decisive_step: Casting and manufacturing of the brake caliper core in China (Scenarios 2 and 3) or the United States (Scenario 1)
flip: Casting and machining the brake caliper core in Mexico rather than merely remanufacturing or assembling it with brake pads.
reasoning: Under CBP precedent (e.g., N336333), the brake caliper core imparts the essential character to a finished brake caliper. Remanufacturing a core and assembling it with brake pads in Mexico does not constitute a substantial transformation into a new and different article of commerce. Therefore, origin is conferred by the country where the caliper core was originally manufactured: China for Scenarios 2 and 3 (FRC11022NP, FRC11021NP), and the United States for Scenario 1 (RC12363P).

key_factors: Refined cane sugar (94.9% by weight)
decisive_step: Cultivation and refining of the sugar, along with final blending in Mexico
flip: Sourcing the refined sugar from a third country like Brazil and blending it in that country before export.
reasoning: Following directly on-point precedent N330744, the product is a dry blend of 94.9% Mexican refined sugar, 4.1% U.S. lactose, and 1% Dutch cocoa powder blended in Mexico. Under the Part 102 hierarchy (specifically 19 C.F.R. 102.11(b)(1)) and substantial transformation principles, the single material that imparts the essential character to the blend is the refined sugar, which overwhelmingly dominates by weight and value and originates wholly in Mexico.

key_factors: Extruded polystyrene foam insulation sheets
decisive_step: Mixing, extrusion, and cutting of raw materials into foam sheets in Canada
flip: If the polystyrene foam sheets were already extruded in the United States or Israel and merely cut to length, printed, and edged with shiplap profiles in Canada.
reasoning: In Canada, raw materials (virgin and recycled polystyrene, talc, colorant from the US and Canada, and flame retardant from Israel) are mixed according to a proprietary formula and extruded under precise temperature and pressure into continuous foam insulation sheets, then cut and edged. Consistent with H290625, compounding and extruding raw plastic resins and additives into finished plastic sheets creates a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use, conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: The base polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film and metallization
decisive_step: Extrusion and metallization of the PET sheet in China
flip: Extruding and metallizing the PET film in the third country where coating or slitting occurs
reasoning: Consistent with CBP precedent N331595 regarding metallized and coated PET film, the essential character of the transfer films (GS-1100, MG-2100, HF-3100, MW-5000) is imparted by the base metallized PET sheet. Subsequent coating (acrylic release, scuff/abrasion-resistant, or pigmented coatings), embossing, or slitting in another country constitutes minor finishing that does not result in a substantial transformation. Thus, origin remains with the country where the PET film is produced, which is typically China in such rulings.

key_factors: Cold pressing of raw seeds and peanuts into liquid vegetable oils
decisive_step: Cold pressing, settling, and filtering of the seeds and peanuts in Canada
flip: Importing pre-extracted crude oil into Canada solely for settling, filtering, and bottling
reasoning: Raw seeds and peanuts from Egypt, China, and Germany (Chapter 12) are imported into Canada and cold-pressed, settled, and filtered into finished liquid culinary oils (Chapter 15, headings 1508 and 1515). Extracting oil from whole seeds/nuts creates a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use (substantial transformation), and satisfies the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rules from Chapter 12 to Chapter 15. Thus, Canada is the country of origin for all three oils.

key_factors: Carbonless copy paper coated with microcapsules and resin-based developers
decisive_step: Manufacturing and chemical coating of the carbonless copy paper in Germany
flip: Manufacturing and coating the carbonless copy paper in Mexico instead of Germany
reasoning: The essential character of the self-copy paper set is imparted by the German-origin carbonless paper, which features specialized chemical coatings (microcapsules and resin-based developers) enabling the image transfer function. Layering the German carbonless paper with Mexican bond paper, rewinding, and cutting to size in Mexico are simple converting and finishing operations that do not substantially transform the German carbonless paper into a new and different article of commerce.

key_factors: LED module (circuit board populated with LEDs)
decisive_step: SMT population of the LED circuit board and driver PCBs in China
flip: Perform the SMT mounting of the LED diodes onto the circuit board in Canada or Mexico
reasoning: In LED lighting rulings (consistent with N325557), the essential character of an LED lamp is imparted by the LED module (the PCB populated with LED diodes) that generates the light. Typically, when Chinese-origin LED modules and driver PCBs are imported into a USMCA country (Canada or Mexico) for final assembly into the lamp tube and end caps, the assembly is considered simple and does not substantially transform the Chinese LED module, leaving China as the country of origin for Section 301.

key_factors: Cold-pressed edible oil
decisive_step: Cold pressing raw nuts and seeds into oil, settling, and filtering in Canada
flip: Cold pressing the U.S. walnuts in the United States and only bottling the oil in Canada
reasoning: Under USMCA marking rules (19 C.F.R. § 102.11) and substantial transformation principles, cold pressing raw nuts and seeds (Chapter 8 or 12) into fixed vegetable oils (heading 1515) in Canada results in a new and different article of commerce and satisfies the tariff shift requirements of 19 C.F.R. § 102.20. Furthermore, hazelnuts and flaxseeds are wholly obtained in Canada. Consistent with companion ruling N351895, the country of origin for all three oils is Canada.

key_factors: 3D-printed molded plastic housing
decisive_step: 3D printing the finished remote holder from PLA filament in Canada
flip: If the remote holder was 3D printed in the filament's country of origin and merely cleaned, painted, or packaged in Canada.
reasoning: In Canada, raw non-originating polylactic acid (PLA) plastic filament undergoes 3D printing to create the finished 'Remote Daddy' remote control holder. Converting raw plastic filament into a specifically shaped, functional protective holder constitutes a substantial transformation, as the filament loses its identity and becomes a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use. Therefore, the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: Guar gum (80% by weight)
decisive_step: Production of the guar gum in Mexico
flip: If xanthan gum from China comprised the majority of the blend by weight and value, imparting the essential character, origin would flip to China.
reasoning: HydroSystem 102P is a simple mixture of 80% Mexican guar gum (heading 1302) and 20% Chinese xanthan gum (heading 3913). Under GRI 3(b), the product is classified in heading 1302 because the predominant guar gum imparts the essential character. Mere dry blending of gums does not result in a substantial transformation into a new article with a distinct name, character, or use, nor does the Mexican guar gum undergo a tariff shift. Thus, the country of origin is Mexico.

key_factors: The cast 14K white gold bracelet links and assembled bracelet body
decisive_step: Casting of the gold links, assembly onto the spring, stone setting, and polishing in Mexico
flip: Performing the casting of the gold links in the United States and only performing minor assembly or polishing in Mexico.
reasoning: Under CBP precedent for jewelry, casting precious metal into jewelry components and assembling the final piece constitutes a substantial transformation. In the United States, only raw materials (alloyed gold grain and stainless steel springs) are produced. In Mexico, the gold is cast into distinct bracelet links, removed from the casting tree, assembled onto the spring wire, set with diamonds (for the first style), and polished, creating a new article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use.

key_factors: Mower deck assembly, gearbox, U.S. engine, and complex final assembly
decisive_step: Stamping and coating the steel mower deck, injection molding plastic components, and assembling all parts with the Mexican gearbox and U.S. engine in Mexico
flip: Manufacturing the mower deck, gearbox, and engine in China and only performing simple screwdriver assembly in Mexico
reasoning: Following precedent N350133 involving the same importer and a nearly identical walk-behind lawn mower, the manufacturing and assembly operations in Mexico—which include stamping and powder coating the steel mower deck, injection molding multiple plastic components, integrating a Mexican gearbox and U.S. engine, and assembling the Chinese components—substantially transform the foreign materials into a new and different article of commerce (and satisfy the Part 102 tariff shift rules for marking), conferring Mexican origin.

key_factors: The printed paper insert containing the scannable video game download code
decisive_step: Printing the scannable download code, cover sheet, and warranty leaflet in the United States
flip: Printing the paper inserts with the scannable codes in Mexico instead of the United States
reasoning: The finished 'code in box' is classified under subheading 4901.10.00, HTSUS, as printed matter. The essential character of the product is imparted by the printed paper insert bearing the scannable video game download code, which is printed in the United States. The operations performed in Mexico—placing the U.S.-origin printed inserts and coversheet into a Canadian plastic retail case and wrapping them—constitute mere simple packaging and do not result in a substantial transformation or tariff shift.

key_factors: Milling and grinding of composite sheets into precision round rods
decisive_step: Cutting, trimming, milling, and grinding the flat sheets into round rods in Mexico
flip: If the raw material imported from India were already extruded or molded in rod form and only underwent minor surface grinding and cutting to length in Mexico
reasoning: The reinforced plastic sheets from India (heading 3920/3921) undergo a multi-step manufacturing process in Mexico—cutting into rectangles, trimming into octagonal blanks, and milling/grinding into precise round profiles. As noted by the classification shift out of heading 3916 to 3926 (other articles of plastics) because the goods are milled and worked beyond a single operation, this processing transforms raw flat composite sheets into a new and different article of commerce (precision rods) with a distinct name, character, and use.

key_factors: LED module blocks (containing LED modules and signal/power PCBA)
decisive_step: Manufacture of the LED module blocks and metal mechanical frame in China
flip: Manufacture the LED modules and LED module blocks in Mexico instead of importing them pre-assembled from China.
reasoning: The Chinese-origin LED module blocks are the most expensive components and perform the core function of displaying visual content, thus imparting the essential character of the display cabinet. Consistent with H304677, where manufacturing the main PCBA in Mexico did not overcome the essential character of the Chinese printer transport, producing the HUB/RC PCBA in Mexico, combined with a simple five-minute final assembly and five-minute firmware upload onto the Chinese frame and LED blocks, does not constitute a substantial transformation.

key_factors: Base conveyor belting (heading 4010.12)
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the vulcanized rubber conveyor belting in Taiwan
flip: Manufacturing the base conveyor belting in Canada rather than importing bulk belting from Taiwan
reasoning: The bulk conveyor belting manufactured in Taiwan imparts the essential character of the finished endless conveyor belts. Both the imported bulk belting and the finished belts are classified under heading 4010 as conveyor belts or belting of vulcanized rubber. Similar to N316637 and N343690, slitting, cutting to length, endless splicing, and vulcanizing Chinese sidewalls and drive lugs onto the Taiwanese base belt in Canada merely customize and finish the belt without creating a new article with a different name, character, or use.

key_factors: The handcrafted white oak barrel body assembled from charred oak staves and steel hoops
decisive_step: Shaping, charring, and cooperage assembly of white oak staves and galvanized steel hoops into complete barrels in Mexico
flip: If the oak staves and heads were pre-shaped, bevelled, notched, and charred in the United States and merely assembled with hoops in Mexico
reasoning: Converting raw lumber and steel strips into coopered, charred oak barrels via cutting, shaping, bending, charring, and hooping creates a new and different article of commerce with a distinct name, character, and use (aging spirits, notably tequila). Under the substantial-transformation test, the country where the cooperage manufacturing and assembly of the oak staves into finished barrels occurs (Mexico) confers origin.

key_factors: Receiver drier subassembly (cylindrical tank with solid core filter and drying agent)
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the receiver drier subassembly in China
flip: Manufacturing the receiver drier tank and solid core filter in Canada instead of China
reasoning: Analogous to N290038, the essential character of the completed receiver drier unit is imparted by the core filtering component—the Chinese-origin receiver drier subassembly (cylindrical tank with internal solid core filter and drying agent). The assembly in Canada, which merely consists of attaching a Chinese pressure switch and a U.S. wire harness to the receiver drier, is a simple combining operation that does not result in a substantial transformation. Therefore, the country of origin is China.

key_factors: Generation of gold waste, scrap, and polishing dust during jewelry manufacturing
decisive_step: Alloying, casting, cutting, and polishing of gold jewelry in Mexico, which yields the resulting waste and scrap
flip: Perform the jewelry casting, cutting, and polishing operations in the United States rather than Mexico
reasoning: The unwrought gold grain from the United States is sent to Mexico where it is alloyed, cast into jewelry, cut from casting trees, and polished. The imported merchandise consists of the excess gold cuttings and polishing dust (classified as gold waste and scrap under heading 7112) derived entirely from these manufacturing operations in Mexico. Because the waste and scrap is derived from manufacturing operations in Mexico and undergoes the applicable tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.20, the country of origin is Mexico.

key_factors: Molded insert body
decisive_step: Molding and shaping of the hockey skate inserts in Canada
flip: If the inserts were molded to final shape in China and only packaged or trimmed in Canada
reasoning: Although the specific manufacturing details were truncated from the facts, hockey skate inserts are frequently designed and molded in Canada (or China) from plastic/foam resins. Forming raw polymer/foam materials into a specifically contoured skate insert creates a new article with a distinct name, character, and use, conferring origin where the molding/forming occurs.

key_factors: The molded ABS plastic doll components (head, torso, arms, legs, and accessories)
decisive_step: Molding of the ABS plastic doll components in China
flip: Molding the main body components (head, torso, limbs) from raw plastic resin in Mexico alongside the final assembly.
reasoning: All components of the doll are molded into their final shapes in China, imparting the article's essential character and predetermined use. The subsequent processing in Mexico consists merely of simple assembly by screwing and gluing pre-formed parts together and retail packaging. Similar to N323116 and N332062, simple assembly of pre-manufactured Chinese components in a USMCA country does not result in a substantial transformation. Therefore, the country of origin remains China.

key_factors: Complete manufacturing and assembly of the electric motor and integration with the fan impeller and housings
decisive_step: Subassembly of the rotor and stator into the electric motor and final assembly of the blower unit in Mexico
flip: Importing a pre-assembled electric motor from China or Japan and performing only simple final assembly with the impeller and housings in Mexico
reasoning: For marking purposes under 19 CFR 102.11 (applicable to USMCA goods) or substantial transformation, even though non-originating housings and impellers (heading 8414) fail the USMCA GN 11 tariff shift rule, the complex manufacturing and assembly of the electric motor (stator/rotor) and final integration of components in Mexico substantially transforms the multi-country parts (Japan, China, US, Mexico) into a new and different article of commerce—a CPAP centrifugal fan blower assembly—conferring Mexican origin for marking and non-preferential purposes.

key_factors: Thermocouple subassembly and complete RF probe fabrication
decisive_step: Manufacturing the thermocouple subassembly (tinning, inserting constantan wire, laser welding into a dome) and assembling the finished RF probe in Mexico
flip: Fabricating the thermocouple subassembly in the United States or South Korea and performing only simple attachment of the handle and cable in Mexico
reasoning: In Mexico, raw stainless steel hypo-tubes (US/South Korea), constantan wire (US), cable (US/China), and connectors (Hungary) undergo complex processing including tinning, laser welding to form a functional thermocouple dome, handle molding, and final electrical assembly. Similar to N330771, this extensive fabrication transforms raw materials and disparate components into a new medical instrument (9018.90, HTSUS) with a distinct name, character, and use, conferring Mexican origin under both substantial transformation and Part 102 marking rules.
